scope: Current shipping desktop, native hub/setup and required release workflows; historical archive workflows and preserved Computer-Link source are not rewritten as a side effect.
status: Dependency choices and official source review; exact release runtime acceptance is recorded by executed hosted release receipts, not this document.

components.name: electron
components.reason: Use the current stable desktop runtime, including upstream renderer/audio and scripted-editor crash fixes.
components.validation: Exact-version Electron startup, integrated desktop workflows and packaged Windows launch must pass on the release source. Cached older local Electron is not acceptance for 45.5.0.

components.name: electron-builder
components.reason: Select the highest stable electron-builder product tag. The repository also releases electron-updater; its /latest result is not the builder version. The intervening stable line includes NSIS extraction and packaging fixes.
components.validation: Rebuild both Windows NSIS and portable artifacts and execute the extracted portable app. Do not adopt the 27 alpha schema migration.

components.name: Node.js build runtime
components.reason: 26.13.1 is the current stable LTS security release. Node 26 entered LTS on October 28. The local 24.22.3 runtime also contains the November security release but remains supplementary compatibility evidence.
components.validation: Current root, desktop, native build tooling and release assembly jobs must run on pinned 26.13.1. Node 25+ Linux binaries need libatomic. Electron's embedded Node version is separate.

components.name: Rust toolchain
components.reason: Current stable 1.100.1 fixes a regression in Iterator trait inference. Use the patch release rather than 1.100.0.
components.validation: Exact-version formatting, strict Clippy, native transport, installer transactions, Windows acceptance and release builds must pass. Local cached 1.99.0 checks are supplementary and do not establish 1.100.1 runtime acceptance.

components.name: Playwright Python
components.reason: Pin the selected current release for reproducible browser fixtures. Upstream 1.65.2 rolls Chromium to 159.0.8154.6.
components.validation: Install the matching Chromium and Firefox distributions. Real installed-extension, hidden-tab and browser smoke gates remain mandatory; a content-script fixture alone is not browser enrollment proof.

components.name: serde
components.reason: Existing exact dependency already matches the latest published stable release.

components.name: serde_json
components.reason: Existing exact dependency already matches the latest published stable release.

components.name: windows
components.reason: The published windows crate remains 0.62.2. Neither the windows-rs repository release label 74 nor an unpublished master Cargo version identifies a replacement crates.io release.

components.name: url
components.reason: A newer published patch requires form_urlencoded 1.2.3. The GitHub /releases/latest endpoint is stale at 2.5.7, so package metadata is authoritative.
components.validation: Both native lockfiles were resolved normally by Cargo. The candidate passed 21 monitor unit/state/wire tests, 12 actual native process/transport tests, all 26 installer transactions, and strict Clippy for Linux and Windows-GNU. Exact hosted release toolchain/runtime acceptance remains separate.

components.name: sha2
components.reason: 0.11.2 is published; it adopts digest 0.11, cpufeatures 0.3 and a Rust 1.88 minimum. Constellation uses SHA-256 for installed/payload byte integrity, so changed digest types and exact lowercase digest output need validation.
components.validation: The first locked compile failed because digest 0.11 output no longer implements LowerHex. Explicit bytewise lowercase hex formatting restores the exact 64-character representation. Standard empty/abc/multiblock and binary vectors pass, including binary equivalence against the old sha2 0.10.9 helper and Python hashlib; all 26 install/repair/rollback tests pass. Upstream SHA-512 speed notes do not establish a Constellation SHA-256 speedup.

nativeIdentity.reason: Align --version with the released application while retaining protocol compatibility.

archiveHandling.nativeSetup: Existing bounded manifest and payload format with byte-count and SHA-256 verification.
archiveHandling.packaging: Python standard-library zipfile and existing desktop/PowerShell archive paths. No unrelated Rust zip dependency introduced.

evidenceBoundaries: Public package/release metadata verifies freshness, not compatibility, speed or runtime acceptance.
No signing, physical sound, user browser enrollment or signed-in account success is inferred from dependency updates.
Keep exact artifact source/version/hash gates and independent Windows runtime checks unchanged.

localNativeDependencyValidation.environment: Linux, cached Rust 1.99.0; isolated candidate copied from the shared release source before mutation.
localNativeDependencyValidation.resolution: Normal Cargo crates.io access resolved and downloaded packages; checksums and transitive lock changes were produced by Cargo, not edited by hand.
localNativeDependencyValidation.initialFailure: sha2 0.11.2 with unchanged payload.rs failed E0277: the digest output no longer implements LowerHex.
localNativeDependencyValidation.repair: payload::hash explicitly encodes each digest byte as two lowercase hex characters; payload framing and recorded digest length remain unchanged.
commands: cargo clippy --manifest-path <each native crate>/Cargo.toml --locked --offline --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings

results.strictWindowsGnuClippy: both crates passed; compile/lint evidence, not Windows execution

binaryDigestEquivalence.input: Every byte value from 0 through 255, in order
references: old sha2 0.10.9 LowerHex helper executed in a separate crate

transitiveChanges.form_urlencoded: 1.2.2 -> 1.2.3 in monitor lock; already 1.2.3 in setup lock

localNativeDependencyValidation.runtimeBoundary: Local Rust 1.99.0 tests and Windows-GNU compilation do not replace the exact pinned Rust 1.100.1 hosted release/runtime gates.

workflowPinAudit.rustPin: 1.100.1 in native-monitor, windows-runtime, windows-setup and computer-tools
workflowPinAudit.playwrightPin: requirements-dev.txt selects exactly 1.65.2 for the browser workflows
workflowPinAudit.correctedGap: computer-tools previously used the hosted image Node; it now installs Node 26.13.1 after the pinned checkout while retaining persist-credentials:false on checkout.
workflowPinAudit.yaml: All six current workflow files parsed successfully with duplicate mapping keys rejected.
workflowPinAudit.electronReadback: windows-runtime reads desktop/package.json after changing into the desktop directory and requires the installed Electron --version to equal v plus the exact dependency pin; its receipt field uses that same source-bound pin.
workflowPinAudit.powershellReview: The parenthesized pipeline/member-access expression is valid as an ordered-hashtable value. This is source review against Microsoft documentation, not a local PowerShell execution result.
workflowPinAudit.focusedRegression: node tests/release-artifacts.test.mjs passed, including individual omission of each of the nine required setup acceptance checks.
workflowPinAudit.sourceProvenance: Reusable release jobs run on the same candidate source; same-run downloads must match version, source commit, file size and SHA-256 before staging. Clean-tree guards and post-publication tag/hash readback remain enabled.
workflowPinAudit.status: Source configuration reviewed; matching hosted run and attached release receipts establish executed acceptance.
